name: PHP
summary: Dynamically typed, reference-counted scripting language originally designed for server-side web templating, with a class-based object model, runtime-enforced type declarations and an RFC-driven evolution process; the Zend Engine in php-src is the reference implementation.

level_notes.0: php-src is the reference implementation: the Zend Engine (Zend/) holds the re2c scanner, Bison grammar, AST compiler, opcode VM (zend_vm_def.h is the template from which the executor is generated), GC and object model; ext/ holds the standard library, ext/opcache the optimizer and JIT. HHVM (see hack), PeachPie (.NET), KPHP and JPHP are alternative implementations of PHP dialects.
level_notes.1: No formal standard. The PHP Language Specification (php/php-langspec, rendered at phplang.org) was written by Facebook/Rex Jaeschke for PHP 5.6/7.0 and is no longer kept current; the php.net Language Reference plus accepted RFCs (wiki.php.net/rfc) describe the current language, and php-src behaviour is definitive.
level_notes.2: No HOPL paper; the manual's History chapter is the main first-party history.
level_notes.3: Rosetta Code reports 'blocked' to automated checkers.
